notes: Discovery: NorthQuay is a platform team inside a major UK bank building enterprise search (internal + customer-facing).
Primary constraint: EU/UK data residency. Must demonstrate London region hosting + Dublin/Frankfurt failover for DR.
Scale: index ~120M documents (approx 350M passages), estimated vector index ~90M vectors after passage split; expected index size ~3.5TB (FP16/quantized target).
Workload: mix of low-latency retrieval (interactive search) and batch reranking for high-value queries. Target p95 retrieval latency <90ms, end-to-end retrieval+rerank <200ms for 95% of queries.
Traffic profile: baseline 180 QPS, peak 800 QPS during market hours; cost sensitivity target: ~€0.005-€0.01 / query (avg) to justify Dedicated capacity commit.

Model preferences: open models vetted first (Llama-family variants), but want Redwood-verified perf profiles. Interested in quantized model variants and dynamic routing to cheaper variants for bulk queries.
Security ask: SSO/SAML integration for developer and admin console, KMS integration (HSM optional), audit logs retention 7 years for compliance team review.
Routing/HA: need multi-region routing policy (latency-first within UK/EU), automatic failover if London capacity constrained, and deterministic fallback to a smaller rerank model if primary fails.

POC acceptance criteria (explicit): 1) <200ms end-to-end on 95% of sample queries; 2) rerank improves MRR by >12% over baseline; 3) demonstration of London residency with audit logs; 4) monthly cost projection within ARR target.
Sales notes: legal asking for specific residency SLA and SOC2 attestation; procurement pushing for 12-month committed pricing to hit ARR target; AE to escalate contract language with pricing team.
Quotes from call: 'If we can't guarantee UK residency and predictable latency we'll keep search in-house' — Head of Platform (call 2025-01-20).
Internal: SE runbook requested — steps for snapshotting index, failover demo, and quantization trade-off sheet (Daniel to deliver by 2025-02-14).
